issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines Ride with an attribute named 'abbreviation' (char), but the solution implements this attribute as 'shortName' with getter getShortName(). This naming discrepancy between the specification (UML) and the solution can confuse students about the expected attribute/getter names and may cause mismatches with tests or instructions that refer to 'abbreviation'.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute name consistent with the UML/problem statement. Rename the Ride attribute and its getter in the solution (and template) from 'shortName' / getShortName() to 'abbreviation' / getAbbreviation(), and ensure the constructor parameter uses the same name and order as in the UML. Alternatively, update the UML/problem statement to use 'shortName' if that naming is preferred and reflect that change everywhere (including task descriptions and tests).

issues.description: The UML in problem_statement.md defines a Ride attribute named 'abbreviation' (char). In the provided solution, the Ride class uses the attribute name 'shortName' (with getter getShortName()). This is a naming mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the ride's short/abbreviated identifier) and may confuse students mapping the UML/problem description to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier across artifacts. Rename the Ride attribute and its getter in the solution from 'shortName'/'getShortName()' to 'abbreviation'/'getAbbreviation()', or update the UML/problem statement to use 'shortName' consistently. Ensure constructors and all references use the chosen name.
